title: Adaptive TPS regression orchestrator and steady-state throughput sentinel
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build an adaptive, production-oriented harness (the 'Throughput Sentinel') that continuously measures model token throughput and P95 latency across representative workloads and automatically flags regressions. This ticket covers design, CI integration, baseline capture, and alerting for core model families (LlamaX-xx, Redwood-v1f, Mosaic-quant variants). The harness must exercise cold and warm KV cache paths, short and long context lengths, and mixed-batch sizes to reflect real traffic shapes. Results should be stored as artifacts and pushed to the throughput dashboard for trend analysis and slicing by model, hardware, and sequence profile.

Key considerations: reproducibility across regions, low measurement noise, capturing steady-state (not just peak TPS), and minimizing cost for nightly runs. We will use deterministic synthetic prompts with seeded randomness and record per-token timings, host/GPU metrics, and kernel selection logs. Regression detection will use a hybrid approach: baseline percent-change thresholds plus a statistical change-point detector to avoid noisy alerts from transient flakiness.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run reproducible throughput scenarios for at least 3 model families and produce per-run artifacts (CSV + JSON + perf traces)
Nightly CI job executes the steady-state scenario (10m steady window) and stores artifacts to s3://redwood-benchmarks/throughput/ (timestamped)
Dashboard ingest pipeline consumes artifacts and shows p50/p95/tokens_per_sec and GPU util per run with history retention of 90 days
Automated regression rule fires when tokens/sec drops >6% AND change-point test p < 0.01, creating a Linear issue with artifacts attached
Regression guard supports opt-out labels for experimental kernels and honors per-model baselines
Documentation and runbook for interpreting alerts plus a reproducibility checklist are published in Confluence
implementation_steps: Define canonical scenarios: short-chat (32 tokens), medium-generation (256 tokens), long-context (2048 tokens) with batch shapes derived from production histograms
Implement runner that sequences warmup -> ramp -> steady-state -> cool-down, capturing per-token timings and KV cache metrics
Add host and GPU telemetry collection (nvidia-smi, DCGM, kernel logs) and map to token timestamps
Create artifact schema and uploader to S3 with run metadata (commit, model, hardware, sequence_profile)
Integrate nightly CI workflow (GH Actions) and nightly retention policy; tag runs by commit and compare to baseline commit
Implement regression detector service: percent-change rules + E-Divisive change-point detection; wire to Alerting (Slack + Linear auto-create)
Build dashboard tiles (Throughput, P95 latency, GPU utilization, Batch efficacy) in internal Grafana and expose URL in artifacts
Author runbook and add 'how to triage' steps including repro CLI command and cost estimate per run
monitoring_and_alerting: Primary alert: 'Throughput regression' - tokens/sec drop >6% and change-point detection confirms shift
Secondary alert: 'Steady-state instability' - p95 latency variance > 30% over 3 consecutive nightly runs
Alert payload includes links to run artifacts, commit, model, hardware, and a suggested first step checklist
Alerts post to #infra-throughput and open a Linear ticket with labels [bench-alert, auto-created]
Silencing: experimental-kernel runs marked with label 'experimental' will not trigger production alerts
risks_and_mitigation: Noisy measurements from shared infra: mitigate by running on isolated Dedicated instances for CI or using dedicated test GPU pool
Non-deterministic model updates: pin model hashes for baseline comparisons and include model-variant metadata
High cost of long steady-state runs: use sampling (run full steady-state for 3 models nightly, lighter smoke for others) and burst only on demand
False positives from kernel scheduler churn: correlate with kernel logs and introduce cooldown window before auto-creating tickets
